Samira K.: hey team — starting this week, trying to get my observability workbench wired up. quick Qs: 1) what's the recommended way to use Datadog API keys for local dev vs k8s? 2) i can't find our service dashboards in Grafana (only Platform Overview) — is there a folder i need access to? 3) Sentry shows "no org access" when I log in. who should I ping to get all three sorted quickly? thanks!

/devex-bot: Welcome to Redwood, Samira! :tada: Please follow the onboarding checklist: https://go.redwood/onboard-checklist and request observability access via the Datadog/Grafana/Sentry quick form. Someone from DevEx will follow up.

Jules (DevEx): hi Samira, welcome! short answers: Datadog -> use a per-user API key kept in 1Password (path: redwood/integrations/datadog/dev). Local: export DD_API_KEY or run the agent in docker; for k8s create a secret and mount it. Grafana -> folders are permissioned, i'll share the team folder with you. Sentry -> invite should be sent to your work email, but i'll re-send if it bounced.

Jules (DevEx): example for k8s secret (helm values speak):
```bash
# create secret from 1Password value (local copy, avoid committing)
kubectl create secret generic datadog-api --from-literal=api-key=$DD_API_KEY -n my-dev-namespace
# helm values snippet
datadog:
  apiKeyExistingSecret: datadog-api
```
Set DD_ENV=dev locally so traces/metrics are tagged and filtered in dashboards.

Ravi (Platform): linked note — Grafana uses SSO groups. i just added you to group "engineers" and shared folder "team/redwood-search". if you still can't see it, logout/login (SSO re-sync) or ping @eng-infra. direct link to folder: https://grafana.redwood/team/redwood-search

Maya (Observability): sent Sentry invite to samira@redwood.com just now — check spam. also FYI: we have a curated dashboard set for new hires called "Starter: Observability" (read-only). If you want edit rights on a specific dashboard, say which and i can grant. For alerts: use tag `team:oncall-search` when creating, otherwise it might default to platform oncall.

Samira K.: thanks all — quick follow-up on billing: if i run the datadog agent locally and send traces, will that incur costs? any config to avoid spamming prod ingestion?

Jules (DevEx): good question — yes ingested traces/metrics count. set sampling low and DD_ENV=dev so we have separate index. you can also run the agent with local-forwarding (no upload) for just UI testing:
```bash
# run agent but don't forward to the cloud (dev quickstart)
docker run --rm -e DD_API_KEY=$DD_API_KEY -e DD_ENV=dev -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock datadog/agent:latest agent run --no-cloud-upload
```
That will keep things local for exploration.

Ravi (Platform): FYI — we also have quota-based safeguards on the dev org, but best practice is to use `dev` env and low sample rates.

Samira K.: i can see the Grafana folder now, and the Sentry invite came through. Datadog secret creation worked (thanks for the kubectl snippet). i'll set sampling low. appreciate the rapid help :raised_hands: 

Maya (Observability): perfect — welcome aboard! if you want, i'll drop a tiny checklist DM with the exact links for dashboards, saved searches, and the onboarding alert playbook.

Samira K.: yes please, a checklist DM would be awesome. closing this thread for now. :slightly_smiling_face:
